s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic and laboratory evidence of myocardial injury, complicated by hypotension
salient_findings: Sudden-onset chest pain with increasing intensity
ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG
Elevation of high-sensitive troponin T level
Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery on emergency angiography
key_facts: The patient is an older woman
The patient has a history of diabetes
The patient has a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain
The intensity of pain increased over time
Initial vital signs showed a normal heart rate and blood pressure
Blood pressure later fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
ECG showed subtle ST-segment elevation in leads V7-V9
ECG showed downward-sloping ST-segment depression in leads V2-V4
High-sensitive troponin T level was elevated at 0.309 ng/mL
Emergency angiography showed thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
Computer tomography angiography revealed contrast present in the myocardium and pericardial effusion
